faq: How much should I charge per square foot for pressure washing?

Most residential jobs land between $0.15 and $0.35 per square foot for flat concrete and $0.20 to $0.45 for house soft washing. Delicate or high surfaces like roofs run higher because they take more care and time.
Should I have a minimum job charge?
Yes. Travel, setup and cleanup cost the same on a tiny job as a big one. Many operators set a minimum between $150 and $250 so small jobs stay worth the trip.
How do I measure a driveway quickly?
Multiply length by width in feet. A typical two-car driveway is about 16 by 38 feet, roughly 600 square feet.

faq: How much do window cleaners charge per pane?

Typical residential rates run about $4 to $8 per pane for inside and outside. Exterior-only service is usually priced lower, and French or divided-light windows are often priced per pane rather than per window.
Do I charge more for second-story windows?
Most window cleaners add $2 to $4 per pane above the ground floor to cover ladder work and the extra time it takes.
What about hard water stains?
Mineral deposits need extra product and scrubbing, so many cleaners add a few dollars per affected pane or quote it separately after seeing the glass.

faq: How much should I charge to mow a lawn?
Many lawn care pros charge $50 to $250 per visit depending on size, or about $0.01 to $0.06 per square foot. A quarter-acre lot often runs $25 to $60 per cut.
Should one-time cuts cost more than weekly service?
Yes. A one-time cut is usually overgrown, harder to schedule and does not repeat, so it is commonly priced 30 to 60 percent above a weekly visit.
How do I convert acres to square feet?
One acre is 43,560 square feet. A quarter acre is about 10,890 square feet, but the mowable lawn is often much smaller once you subtract the house, drive and beds.

title: House Cleaning Price Calculator (Free) | Field Quote Kit
desc: Free house cleaning price calculator. Quote standard, deep and move-out cleans from home size, condition and your hourly rate, then copy a quote to send.
lede: Quote standard, deep and move-out cleans by the time they really take. Enter the home, pick the condition, set your hourly rate per cleaner, and the estimate updates as you type.
how: Labor hours start from square footage, plus time for each bathroom and bedroom.
A deep clean is figured at about 1.75 times a standard clean and a move-out at about 2 times.
Condition and pets add time for buildup and pet hair; add-ons add fixed time.
Hours are priced at your hourly rate per cleaner, plus supplies and travel, then the minimum applies.
faq: How much should I charge per hour for house cleaning?

Published guides put typical US rates at about $30 to $80 per hour per cleaner. Your rate needs to cover your pay plus self-employment taxes, insurance, supplies and unpaid time like driving and quoting, so many owners set a target of $40 to $60.
How much more should a deep clean cost?

A deep clean usually takes 1.5 to 2 times as long as a standard clean of the same home, so it should cost about that much more. Whole-home deep cleans commonly run $180 to $375 in published pricing guides.
How much do move-out cleans cost?
Move-in and move-out cleans are often priced around $220 to $400 for a typical home, because they cover inside cabinets, appliances and areas regular cleans skip.
Should I quote a flat price or charge by the hour?
Most clients prefer a flat quote so they know what they will pay. Use the hours behind the scenes to set that flat price, so the quote stays simple and you still earn your hourly rate.
